content.label: The app is amazing at first looks. It has a beautiful design, tour, and interactive great features. The only problem though is that if you have different devices, you have to pay again and more. The price for iPhone is $9.99, but then the Mac version is $49.99. It would be great if you were able to buy it on one device and have it on the rest. But either way, great app. 🙂
The feature that would give it the ultimate perfect app is if it integrated with Alexa.

I have been using Things for approximately 10 years. I have ventured off to other reminder, projects & to do list apps for more customizations. I found I spent more time playing with bells and whistles and complex moves in an attempt to be more productive. Culture Code has made an indispensable app that keeps planning workflow to basics with small customization and integration with iOS apps that feel big in the scheme of planning and productivity. Thank you for a great app!!!!

It’s really absurd that it’s impossible to convert tasks into subtasks. For years I’ve tried to embrace Things into my workflow, but every time I get back to using it I get reminded immediately why I’d never used it for longer than a week before.

If I have any number of tasks 3, 8, 15.. and I decide to convert them into subtasks i.e. group them within a single parent task, there is no way to do so.

It wouldn’t even import subtasks from Reminders!
All reminders subtasks get imported as individual tasks, and I have to manually copy tens of tasks one by one and paste them as tasks one by one.

What an awful and unpleasant experience.

It’s really incredible how such a wonderful and powerful app gets completely crippled by this flaw that renders it unusable to me. I have Things installed on my iPhone, iPad, Mac & Apple Watch. Just sitting pretty collecting digital dust because it’s a productivity nightmare.

I wish the developers would reconsider & deliver this essential feature as an update in a near future. There are paid users like myself that have nought every version of this up & haven’t gotten their money’s worth from the app.

title.label: Amazing! But .. I wish I could collaborate

content.label:
Things is an absolutely amazing app with a beautiful interface and intuitive design. I have tried all the to do list apps on the market and this one is my best. It has just enough features without overwhelming the user with too many choices. I also love that it’s a to do list app - nothing more. 

That said, I would pay money to have the ability to collaborate on a to do list with one other person. I don’t need something for a team of people, but rather a way to share a Project with my partner. We are planning a wedding right now and using this app to do it. However, we both wish there was a way to work on the wedding project together aside from sending markup texts back and forth. This feature would benefit so many households without making it into some kind of project management team tool. Please find a way to make this happen!

I love this app, it is exactly what I need… but I would really really love if they added the ability to take a photo or a screenshot and send to Things as a stand-alone task… it is the single missing function that would vastly improve my productivity!
Things 3 is a great, increase the proclivity by organizing steps of the project. The thing that I wish in the app is the ability to save Area/project/To-Do as template to be reused once need it

I will give five stars when I can use this on my Windows computer as well. I had to leave finally after years for Todoist. I have been a mess not being able to access my planner everywhere. Very sad :(
I would like to see the current date on the “today” screen.  I was on the “today” screen and found myself checking my watch for the current date.

I have tried so many adhd apps and bought so many planners and never stuck with anything. But Things 3 definitely made my life simpler! I planned and organized an upcoming move, my career ladder, and added some personal goals too. You can organize just about anything.

Because of the adhd I have such a poor working memory, so I appreciate I can just add things to my inbox and review them daily to see what I can tackle.

Being able to accomplish my goals has boosted my self esteem and allows me to gain discipline over my life in spite of my neurodivergent brain :)

title.label: It’s $80 to have things on other mac devices

content.label:
It’s a good todo list that BUT I don’t appreciate having to pay $50 extra for the Mac app and another $20 for the iPad app when there are other alternatives, that will give me access across all devices, including android for one price.

$80 for a to do list is a bit much other than that, it’s an excellent to do list that’s well designed and really is helping me be more productive
I don’t like tho how you can’t complete a task early that’s on repeat

title.label: Great, but widgets and complications don’t update

content.label: The app is great. The widgets and complications don’t update unless you click on them which defeats the purpose of having them. Really hard for me to give this a 4 star.

After trying a number of different to-do apps, I found that Things 3 works best for me. It’s clean, easy to use, and the way you can organize makes so much sense. I also appreciate that you can sync it with other apps, including my calendar. I’d strongly recommend this app to artists that have multiple projects and deadlines. Plus it’s not an eyesore like other apps. The only things I wish they would add is a photo feature. It would be so helpful to add sketches/documents to my projects. Also wish there was a student discount for the mac version! Either way I’ll be saving up in the mean time :)

title.label: Excellent App but needs critical improvement to avoid being money sink

content.label:
I would readily pay all $80 the developers want from us for this app suite! It is overall excellent and exactly what I was looking for in a to-do app. However, when I purchase a suite such as this, I assume that I will be able to use it at its current level of functionality for several years -- to put it on the same price level as $30/year subscription services like its peers. When things 3 came out, the developers dropped support for syncing in things 2! This is absolutely unacceptable as if I didn't want syncing I would not pay the extra $30 for the iPhone and iPad apps. I do not expect the developers to maintain expensive servers indefinitely, however. 

The developers need to add support for syncing over iCloud like most other syncing apps on the App store, or my rating will remain low as I expect upon the advent of things 4, sync support will once again be dropped. This would allow users to use the $80 software suite that they paid for for as long as they choose, and purchase the new version if they feel the features so warrant it, not because the developers feel as though it is appropriate to extort users by disrupting their use of the existing software.

I desperately want to be able to endorse this app wholeheartedly, to make it my daily driver and say it’s indispensable to my life. I can’t. The pace of development is glacial and, despite its good looks, it’s lacking in standard features — shared lists, assigning — that are pro forma on other apps.
Works great for me
The desktop version has natural language, but the mobile app doesn’t; it’s a little tedious to manually add a date using the date picker instead of typing it in the task.
I love things, but I hate that it doesn’t integrate with anything. Like Fantastical. Or Notion. Or Zapier.
Decent but the reminder is garbage. The UX for reminder is so backwards, I actually use the built in apple reminders for anything time sensitive. This is sad because apple typically has awful apps.
You will like it, excited to try the desktop ver in the future.
Get it. It’s worth the money. Doesn’t overwhelm you. It’s simple and has every tool you need with none you don’t.

This is the first time I’ve actually had fun managing my daily tasks. I use things to boil down my larger business task lists into manageable, daily chunks. The app works well and syncs between all my devices, and it’s enjoyable to use. Bravo devs.
If you’re looking for the best way to organize, this is it. No other app is as complete, simple, and intuitive as Things 3. I promise. This is what you’re looking for. I promise. 👍

This app would be perfect if it weren’t for the lack of time blocking ability. Why not be able to put the start and finish of a particular event? If I have a work meeting on my to-do list that goes from 1pm-2pm then the only thing I can do is put work meeting on my to-do list in a vague manner. Sad, really.
Does what it’s supposed to do. Mostly easy to navigate except few instances (like subheadings). Could have more features.

Best to-do app i’ve found. Quite pricey but i don’t regret the purchase. It’s simple and effective.  However, there is one big issue: you can’t make a heading in an area. I don’t understand why this is not a feature. There are many tasks that fall within an area that aren’t part of a project. For example, if my area is home and i need to remember to buy more dish soap and to buy a new phone charger, these are things i would like to put under the heading “things to buy” under the area “home” but i don’t want this to be a project. Instead now all your misc tasks float around with each other in an area and it looks very messy. It would be simple to program in this option and the community has been asking for it for years but the developers won’t budge. I’ll stick with things 3 for now but this is the one silly little thing that is making me not fully in love with the app.
I have tried a lot of task managers and Things 3 is by far the most useful and beautiful. No gimmicks or bloating, let’s you focus on the tasks you need to accomplish.

This app has truly changed my life, and that is not an exaggeration. I have been using this for years now, and I am not sure how I functioned without it. I am a “forgets unless I write it down” person, and having this app easily accessible on my phone has been a game changer. There is so much you can do, I know I’m not even using it to its full ability. GET THIS APP! It is 100% worth it.

title.label: Apple’s free Reminders app is better.

content.label: Why would you not allow associating specific time to tasks? There is no way of automatically arranging recurring daily tasks that I need to complete at 8AM, 9AM, and 10AM in that order for example. There is also no way to create tasks that only occur on weekdays or only on Tuesdays and Thursdays. I can’t believe I paid $10 for this. Apple’s free Reminders app is better.

This app is helping me organize my life, things I would usually forget. Instead of procrastinating, I have a future folder that is able to remind me of due dates, projects, and tasks I usually just store in the back of my brain!

title.label: Wish I Could Get My Money Back…

content.label: Overall, the app is nice. The main reason why I bought it is because it can be used across multiple apple products (my iPhone, iPad, Mac, and watch are all connected). I purchased this app for my phone and want to use it with my Mac. I get in to use it (because I think it would be faster to input my to do list with my Mac than my cell phone and it cost FIVE TIMES MORE to use the EXACT SAME APP on my computer. WHAT THE F? So I can’t use it on anything but my phone. You have to pay for the exact same thing to use on a different platform, what a scam! 😡
This is the world’s best development and UX team. I’m in awe of how many small things are delightful.

title.label: Task Creation Date?? Repeat feature fix

content.label:
1) Unless I’m missing something, there is no way to see when you created a task. If there is please share. If not, please add this feature. Also perhaps a “date edited”. So “date created” and “date edited”. 
2) When creating a task (tapping the + or using Force Touch in app icon) there is no way to set it to repeat. You can only do that after you create the task, which is a pain especially if you add a date to it. Because then you have to search for the task, find it, then go in and set a repeat. JUST ADD THE REPEAT OPTION WHEN CREATING A NEW TASK.
3) Lower the Mac OS price. I run Things on iPhone and iPad and refuse to pay $50 so end up having to grab my phone when I’m on my Mac and need to create a task I thought of.

Simple and intuitive to you, but powerful under the hood. Within a few hours I was able to set up a hyper efficient workflow to manage several personal projects. I immediately bought the iPad and Mac versions and this has proven to be a wise investment, despite the seemingly high price. Cannot recommend more, it’s simply fantastic.
This a great app to organize your todos. Easy to learn. Cloud based to work across multiple Macs and iPhone. If you like Asana, you will like this.
I just bought the app and deleted it. I need a refund. How do I request for a refund. Not what I wanted.

title.label: Would be 10+ stars with just one added feature

content.label: I have use this app for as long as I can remember, I have it for my iPhone, iPad, and computer. It is simply the best to-do and organizational app out there. None  beat it and I tried them all. The only thing it is lacking is the ability to share a to do list with another Things user. I should be able to share a to do list with my husband (for example)i f he has a Things account too. The lack of this feature is, unfortunately, making me look elsewhere. Please, please add this feature ASAP. I'm not sure why after all these upgrades and versions, it still doesn't have the feature to simply share a list or project with another person and work collaboratively.

Interface and design is nice BUT you can’t attach files, photos, contacts, or maps: Biggest thing from stopping me from leaving 2Do for Things. 
Also, you should have the calendar view on the widget also, or it’s the widget is half-useless.
Add these features, and I won’t keep coming back to Things and then leaving because I forgot why I left.

This app has everything you need and nothing extra -- which is better in my book than some more complex solutions like 2Do and OmniFocus. Things 3 doesn't get in the way of productivity like some other task management apps do because it's fast to enter tasks, gives you just the right amount of additional features, and has a beautiful UI that simply makes sense.
Wasted my money, thank u

Not much to say really. I have been using Things 3 to keep my life in order for years. It’s an absolute joy to use, and I look forward to using for years to come. One of the best pieces of software I’ve ever seen.

Update nov 13,22- they did it again! I’m in middle of 4 day seminar with 750 people & Things scrambles my everyday list with high priority today list even tho I had them separate. Apple why are you ignoring this? Will nake a great article or post on Twitter! Previous-Was my go to for years, however after being chastised by developer that I had “too many to do’s” (seriously?) I’ve been less than impressed.  Tried others and was on the fence about switching. Wrote in recenty (1st time in almost 3 yrs) w/ quick question. Tho recd answer, suddenly whole thing not just wonky, THEY MIXED MY CAREFULLY PRIORITIZED REPEATING TASKS WITH THE ONE-OFFS!!! And do a Re-mix nightly!! No more fence. Would sue if I could. Am White House journalist, recovering from sudden death of my husband & concomitant legal/financial crises in the wake of his passing, have Post Concussion Syndrome… and these guys are purposely messing with my productivity? (Yes they knew that upfront when I’d responded to the “too many to do’s” I’d foolishly explained, hoping for cooperation since zero compassion) (As a clergyperson I know says, “don’t want to be standing with them in an electric storm.”) Very bad karma, guys Hello Tick, Tick!
What a ripoff. Doesn’t do anything a free app can’t do, and didn’t do what I needed, which was grab my attention and keep me from missing important reminders.
Please add a “all” view. It’s simple and intuitive. Quick and easy way to do things (no pun intended).

title.label: Good app ruined by the tracking policy

content.label: Why does it need access to user content?!

The app is extremely inconvenient and unfriendly.  It is impossible to add the duration and time of the task, there is no event detail, there is no task location.  Not worth a money, extremely dissatisfied

title.label: Reminded me hours after the reminder

content.label: What good is a reminder app that reminds you hours after the reminder is set for?

Can you please add repeating tasks with deadlines for a specific date or at least a reminder a month ahead instead of just 14 days before the same deadline?
Because I have a monthly task which is due for the same month but I want a reminder every month on the first day and a due date at the last day of the month

As a scientific researcher who has to plan out experiments far I. Advance with specific dates, this app is AMAZING. The one wish I have is that when I schedule tasks ahead of time that they would show up on my calendar immediately as well. I feel like if you could create a calendar subscription link that did this the app would be literal perfection. PLEASE PLEASE make this happen 🥺🙏🙏🙏
